lawyer:
Md. Selim Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Mahmuda Begum, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent

The State represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong----Petitioner
Vs.
Hussain Ahmed Sakik @ Moulana Hossain Md. Youns -------- Respondent
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J.: This criminal petition is by the State-petitioner for leave to appeal from the judgment and order dated 26.08.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8993 of 2006 making the Rule absolute and quashing the proceeding of G.R. No. 602 of 2005 arising out of Bakalia Police Station Case No. 08 dated 16.08.2005 under sections 406/420/465/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 3. The case, made out in the FIR, in short, is that on 06.03.2005 Md. Reza, son of late Isha, Administrative Officer, Al-Jamea Al-Islamia, Police Station-Potiya, Chittagong, filed a complaint petition before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong against the accused-petitioner and another, Subsequently the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, by an order, directed to register the complaint petition as an F.I.R. The complainant has alleged that after the devastating cyclone of the 29th April, 1991, some respectable persons on 16.05.1999, established Islamic Relief Committee Peoples Welfare Institution and father of accused petitioner No. 1 had been nominated as its President. After that, in the name of said relief committee, an account was opened in the Bank of accused No. 2 and that the President was appointed as an operator of the account. On 14.02.1992, the President died and during his life time there were 25 transactions in that account. On 16.02.1992 , the Secretary, Moulana Harun Islamabadi in presence of accused No. 1 and with the consent of all was nominated as the president of the Committee. It was unanimously decided that the Bank account in the name of committee would be operated by the President and two others. The resolution of the said meeting was forwarded to the bank of accused No. 2 but in collusion with accused No. 1, he refused to operate the Bank account. Lastly, accused No. 1 gave him mandate and a copy of the resolution was handed over to the accused No. 2 but meanwhile owing to his non co-operation Tk. 57,00,000/- was withdrawn by forgery and fraud by the accused. The complainant became astonished to see how the bank authority could make transaction beyond the legal operator. The power of mandate ceased with the death of person giving the mandate. On 15.02.2002 the Bank authority got the information of death. The accused persons by using invalid mandate of the dead man misappropriated a huge amount of money and did not return same in spite of the separate demands. Accused No. 1 tried to misappropriate Tk. 51 lacs from the accounts of Eastern Bank’s Agrabad Branch and Agrani Bank’s Patiya Branch but the order of the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong, in Miscellaneous Case No. 129 of 1994 could stop such transaction. The complainant has taken all possible steps to stop the bank transactions but because of the authority of the said band it could not be done. They tried to recover the money till 05.03.2005. Subsequently, an F.I.R. was lodged with the Bakalia Police Station resulting in Bakalia P.S. Case No. 08 dated 16.08.2005. 

 4. Police took up investigation and submitted charge-sheet against the accused and another under sections 406/420/465/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code, since prima-facie case was made out against them. 

 5. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the framing charge under sections 406/420/465/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code, the accuse filed Miscellaneous Case No. 8993 of 2006 before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding of Bakalia Police Station Case No. 08 dated 16.08.2005 now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong and obtained Rule Nisi. 

 6. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 26.08.2009 made the Rule absolute quashing the proceeding of G.R No. 602 of 2005 arising out of Bakalia P.S. Case No. 08 dated 16.08.2005 now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong.
